name: Alfalfa
grown_as: A deep-rooted perennial grown as green manure, fodder or sprouting seed; also found wild on field edges. Also called lucerne. Flowers range from lilac to deep violet.
habit: An upright, bushy perennial 30 to 90 cm, many stems from a woody crown, from a very deep taproot. Stems smooth to slightly downy. Dies back to the crown in winter.

leaf.leaflets: The middle leaflet on a short stalk of its own, the two side ones almost stalkless. All roughly symmetrical.
leaf.outline: Each leaflet narrowly obovate to oblong, 1 to 3 cm, widest toward the tip
leaf.tip: Squared off or slightly notched, with a tiny point
leaf.margin: Small sharp teeth only near the tip; the lower part of each leaflet without teeth
leaf.veins: Straight side veins running into the teeth
leaf.stalk: Short (1 to 2 cm); narrow pointed stipules, toothed at their base

flower.form: Small pea flowers packed into a short dense spike
flower.colour: Violet to purple, sometimes lilac or bluish
flower.behind: A small downy calyx with five narrow teeth
flower.carried: 10 to 40 flowers in a short oblong head 1 to 4 cm on a stalk from the leaf joints, held up above the leaves

fruit: A small downy pod coiled into a flat spiral of 2 to 3 turns with a hole in the middle, like a tiny snail shell, green ripening brown-black. Seeds tiny, kidney-shaped, yellow-brown, about 2 mm.
seedling: Two small oval seed leaves on short stalks, then a first true leaf with a single rounded leaflet, then three-leaflet leaves.
winter: Dies back to a woody crown at the soil; dead stems may stand

leaf: three narrow leaflets, the middle one on a short stalk
teeth only near the leaflet tips
bloom: a short dense oblong head of small pea flowers
on a stalk from a leaf joint
seed: a tiny kidney-shaped seed, about 2 mm
young: an upright leafy clump of many stems
flower: short violet flower heads held just above the leaves
seedhead: small pods coiled in a flat spiral of 2 to 3 turns
dormant: a woody crown at the soil
dead stem stubs, little or nothing green

look_alikes: Black medick (Medicago lupulina) is low and sprawling with tiny yellow heads and black kidney pods. Clovers have round heads and leaflets toothed all round, with no stalk on the middle leaflet. Sickle medick (M. falcata) has yellow flowers and sickle-shaped pods.
